angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 257,200 km at 72.56 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 13.7808 +/- 0.0267 mas (same row, RUWE 1.31): 72.56 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.3697 +/- 0.016 solar radii from Hobson et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-3235 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJ...946L...4H/abstract): 257,200 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.3939 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Hobson et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-3235 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJ...946L...4H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3388.8 +/- 68 K from Hobson et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-3235 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJ...946L...4H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Hobson et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-3235 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJ...946L...4H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-3235.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.898, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-3235 (pscomppars): spectral type M V, from Hobson et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJ...946L...4H/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-3235 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.264 dex, from Hobson et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJ...946L...4H/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-3235 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.78968, from Hobson et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJ...946L...4H/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
